PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/07/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent cough with yellow sputum and fatigue not significantly improved since last visit.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit one week after extending his course of Azithromycin and initiating oral Prednisone for his COPD exacerbation. He reports that while his cough remains productive with yellow sputum, he has not observed any substantial improvement in his overall fatigue or respiratory symptoms. The patient states that the wheezing persists, particularly during exertion, and he continues to experience shortness of breath while performing daily activities. He has noted no new symptoms such as fever or hemoptysis but expresses concern over his lack of improvement.
Mr. Fairfax has been compliant with his medication regimen, including the use of nebulized albuterol every hour as needed. He has maintained his symptom diary, documenting the frequency and nature of his cough and sputum, which he reports to be consistent with previous observations.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, - weight loss, - fever, - chills, - night sweats. Pulmonary - + productive cough with yellow sputum, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 132/78 mmHg - Heart Rate: 82 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 26 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 88% on room air.
General: The patient appears fatigued and slightly distressed.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Moderate wheezing noted on auscultation; increased bronchial breath sounds; rhonchi heard bilaterally; prolonged expiration.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with persistent exacerbation; inadequate response to current treatment regimen evidenced by ongoing productive cough and fatigue. 2. Congestive heart failure stable; no signs of fluid overload. 3. Persistent fatigue likely multifactorial, exacerbated by ongoing respiratory symptoms and underlying cardiac condition.
PLAN
1. Discontinue Azithromycin given lack of clinical improvement and consider potential for antibiotic resistance; initiate a trial of oral Levofloxacin 750 mg daily for 7 days to address possible bacterial infection. 2. Continue oral Prednisone 20 mg daily for an additional 5 days to manage inflammation associated with COPD exacerbation. 3. Introduce a long-acting beta-agonist (LABA), specifically Salmeterol 50 mcg twice daily, to enhance bronchodilation and improve respiratory function. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every hour as needed; monitor for any adverse effects or increased frequency of use. 5. Schedule follow-up in one week for reevaluation of respiratory status, sputum characteristics, and overall fatigue levels. Consider pulmonary function testing if symptoms do not show significant improvement.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was discharged home with a revised prescription for oral Levofloxacin and continued Prednisone therapy. He was advised to maintain his symptom diary and to utilize nebulized albuterol as needed. A follow-up appointment has been scheduled for one week from today to assess the effectiveness of the new treatment regimen and to further refine his management plan based on clinical response.
